correctness.rationale: All graph-ball branches are written explicitly. The operator T has two zero-sum singular values and a 2D Perron singular block of trace tau and determinant 1/(a+1)^2. A uniform max-output bound implies X^2>=a-20(a+1)^3/sqrt(b) at any maximizing unit input. The stated threshold forces strict radius-0 choices on the a-side and strict radius-1 choices on the b-side; thus every maximizing input falls in the linear T region, establishing the sharp global nonlinear norm and equality cases. The asymptotic follows by a justified positive quadratic-root expansion. The finite checker replayed 2658 assertions, but universal validity is from the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The strong ell_2 norm of centered graph-ball maximal functions is a classical nontrivial problem even on finite graphs, with exact star/complete results but no general graph formula in the inspected papers. The theorem provides the exact nonstar biclique constant throughout an infinite, mathematically natural extreme-imbalance regime, all maximizing moduli, and the first inverse-size correction. Its nontrivial localization lemma reduces the nonlinear competition among three ball radii to a unique two-class singular-value configuration. The threshold is nonoptimal but explicit; the result is not merely a sampled norm or a relabeling of the already covered star case.
